blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Invariant Closure**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

Each axis of the H·S·A space names a way an autonomous run can fail: an agent with write authority can touch the wrong resource, carried state can accumulate silent corruption, and a multi-turn trajectory can end with a fluent claim that the job is done while the defect remains live. Because the model cannot vouch for the safety or correctness of its own outputs, the surrounding runtime must close those exposures from outside the model.

blocks.title: What the section covers
blocks.md:
In the book this section runs through:

- The fail-plausible fault
- The invariant closure principle
- The five-part task contract

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Task contract matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A goal with negative scope, an environment, permitted actions, available observations, and completion criteria turn intent into something the runtime can enforce, and each omitted field produces a specific, predictable failure.

questions.q: The section **Invariant Closure** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Authority levels A0 to A3 (read-only, disposable workspace, compensable, irreversible) classify an action by its consequence in the environment, and the same command can change class when the environment changes.
The characteristic agent failure is well-formed, credible, and wrong, so fail-stop monitors record success and agreement among samples from one model sets no bound on wrong answers.
Constraints never rest on the model: bounds close mechanically below it and acceptance rests on external evidence above it, and greater exposure demands stronger closure.

A goal with negative scope, an environment, permitted actions, available observations, and completion criteria turn intent into something the runtime can enforce, and each omitted field produces a specific, predictable failure.
